title: Useful Phrasal Verbs for Work
summary: Learn three common phrasal verbs to talk about daily office tasks. Boost your professional English vocabulary easily.

sections.p: When you start something new, like a meeting, a room, or a computer system, you set it up. It means to prepare or arrange everything so it is ready to use.

ex.en: Can you please set up the projector for the meeting?
I need to set up a new email account for our new colleague.
ex.mean: I need to create and prepare a new email.

sections.p: To carry out means to do a task, plan, or study from the beginning to the end. We often use it for research, tests, or instructions.

ex.en: The team will carry out a survey to check customer happiness.
ex.mean: The team will do a survey.

ex.en: She always carries out her manager's instructions quickly.
ex.mean: She always does what her manager asks.

sections.p: To follow up means to contact someone again, or to do more action after a first meeting or message. It shows you are active and interested.

tip: Try to link each phrasal verb to a real task you do at work every week. Writing your own sentences helps your brain remember them faster.

quiz.en: We need to ___ a meeting room for our guests tomorrow morning.
The technicians will ___ repairs on the office printer this afternoon.
Please ___ with the supplier to see if the goods have been shipped.
It takes twenty minutes to ___ the computer before the presentation starts.
The researchers plan to ___ interviews with fifty different employees.
After sending the proposal, I will ___ with a phone call next week.
